text:
Marissa Cole: ok, need to lock rollout plan for customer-visible model changelog. proposal: phased rollout (private beta -> GA) w/ clear success metrics + timeline. can folks sanity check?

Paula Mendes: +1. also need to make sure Rollouts UI can link to “published as-of change time” notes, otherwise this is gonna create more confusion.

Dylan Brooks: agree. also want to avoid the “half shipped” thing where docs has it but Console doesn’t, or vice versa.

Marissa Cole: rough phases:
1) internal dogfood (Redwood employees only)
2) private beta: 3–5 enterprise accounts (opt-in)
3) GA: all hosted + dedicated (private later if needed)

Marissa Cole: private beta accounts shortlist from CS: FinchBank, HelioHealth, StackForge (maybe 1–2 more). they’re the loudest about change management.

Dev Patel: yup those are the ones. they want: (a) immutable/auditable notes (b) linkable URL per model version (c) “what changed” in plain english.

Chloe Martin: gating-wise easiest is feature flag + account allowlist on Console backend + feed endpoint rate limit.

Connor O'Brien: need to map to release trains. we can’t be publishing new customer surfaces during freeze windows unless it’s behind flag and already deployed. so we should treat “GA flip” like a release.

Elliot Price: docs side: we can ship the release notes pages behind a hidden nav entry (or non-indexed) during beta. GA = add nav + docs landing page + RSS/Atom link.

Tessa Morgan: design wants at least 1 week of beta usage before we bless UI. otherwise we’ll miss obvious UX holes (filters, share link, compare view).

Kenji Nakamura: +1. also workflow copy/labels matter (draft vs in review vs published). I’d rather learn w/ 3 customers than at GA.

Marissa Cole: cool. timeline suggestion (tentative):
- Week 0 (next sprint): internal dogfood in staging + prod (employees only)
- Week 2: private beta in prod (allowlist)
- Week 4–5: GA decision + enable for all orgs (hosted + dedicated)

Paula Mendes: can we call out “GA criteria” explicitly? otherwise we’ll argue in week 4.

Marissa Cole: yes. proposed GA criteria:
- 95%+ of model version changes have a published changelog entry within 24h
- publish lag p50 < 2h, p95 < 24h (excluding manual holds)
- <1% of entries require post-publish correction (measured weekly)
- Console: model page loads w/ changelog tab error rate <0.5%
- Support: no increase in “model changed without notice” tickets; ideally reduction vs baseline

Owen Phillips: for support readiness, i’d add: “support playbook + known gaps doc exists” and “CSMs have a one-pager on how to subscribe to feed + where to find pinned version.”

Dev Patel: +1. also define what counts as a “correction” (typo vs material change). otherwise metric gets noisy.

Connor O'Brien: publish lag should exclude freeze windows? bc during RC we might intentionally hold publish.

Marissa Cole: good call. we can track both:
- “generator lag” (event -> draft)
- “time to publish” (event -> published)
…and report with tags: held_for_review, freeze_hold.

Chloe Martin: for metrics, Logan/observability was drafting dashboard panels. we can instrument:
- event_ingest_success
- template_render_fail
- docs_publish_fail
- approval_queue_age
- broken_link_rate (Console -> docs)

Dylan Brooks: biggest failure mode i worry about is missing entries due to schema validation blowups. can we have a beta rule: if generator fails, we show a banner + fallback to “raw change event summary” internally? for customers maybe “Release note pending”?

Elliot Price: docs doesn’t want raw diffs ever visible. “Release note pending review” is ok, but we need a max window. also should include “how to contact support” link.

Naomi Feldman: from compliance side: for beta, we need to be careful on wording like “immutable.” we can say “tamper-evident history” internally, but customer-facing should be “published entries are versioned and prior versions remain accessible” (or whatever security signs off).

Marissa Cole: ok, we’ll avoid promising immutability in marketing copy until security review is done.

Paula Mendes: what about Private deployments? enterprise will ask.

Dylan Brooks: I’d keep Private out of GA scope. we can say “planned” and focus on hosted/dedicated first. Private has different docs/upgrade cadence.

Marissa Cole: agreed. beta can include 1 dedicated customer and 1 hosted-only. Private = phase 2.

Kenji Nakamura: approvals: who’s the final approver in beta? if we make it too heavy it’ll slow publish and we’ll miss metrics.

Marissa Cole: beta approval SLA proposal:
- default: Support readiness (Dev) + Product (Marissa/Paula delegate) async signoff
- sensitive entries (deprecation / behavior change): add Release Eng (Connor) + Compliance reviewer (Naomi) within 1 business day

Connor O'Brien: ok as long as we have an emergency publish path for corrections.

Chloe Martin: workflow states already support that: draft -> in_review -> published. we can add “expedite” flag that pings approvers.

Dev Patel: for private beta comms: we should send customers a short “what to expect” + how to give feedback. also set expectations: historical release notes may be incomplete until backfill.

Elliot Price: + include a style baseline: “Impact / Compatibility / Deprecation timeline / Links”. if beta entries are inconsistent, customers will call it out.

Tessa Morgan: also want a feedback loop: 30-min weekly check-in with beta accounts + quick form for “confusing wording” reports.

Marissa Cole: success metrics for beta specifically:
- at least 2/3 beta accounts confirm this unblocks their change management process (qual)
- <5 customer-reported confusion issues per week after week 1
- 0 P0 incidents caused by showing wrong version/changelog link

Owen Phillips: can we add a metric for “pinning usage”? like % of calls that include model_version pin after we start surfacing it in Console/API.

Dylan Brooks: yep. adoption signal we want.

Chloe Martin: note: API/SDK surfacing might lag Console by a sprint. should we gate GA on that?

Marissa Cole: I think GA for Console + docs can proceed, but we’ll label API/SDK as “coming soon” in beta. For GA, requirement is at least API response header includes resolved version + changelog url on main OpenAI-compatible routes.

Connor O'Brien: ok. release plan:
- ship everything behind flag in the next train
- enable internal dogfood immediately
- beta enable mid-train after we see stability
- GA flip at start of next train

Paula Mendes: + make sure Rollouts uses published entry id, not “latest,” otherwise audit is broken.

Chloe Martin: already in the plan: rollouts store changelog_entry_id at time of change.

Marissa Cole: action items:
- Marissa: write rollout plan + GA criteria into PRD + share w/ exec staff channel
- Chloe: confirm feature flag + allowlist mechanics + broken link banner behavior
- Connor: map to freeze windows + suggest GA flip date
- Dev/Owen: draft beta customer comms + support enablement checklist
- Elliot: confirm docs beta mode + nav/rss GA switch

Marissa Cole: if no objections by EOD, i’ll treat this as the plan and we’ll start lining up the beta accounts.

Dylan Brooks: :thumbsup:

Paula Mendes: :thumbsup: pls add a note that we’ll do a rollback plan (disable flag + keep history).

Marissa Cole: yup, adding “rollback = disable flag + keep published entries accessible via direct link” + “corrections use superseding entry.”
